records.label: Patient 1690
quotes: analysis of the exome of patient 1690 (South Asian), with 5 CHMs, 3 MCs, 1 stillbirth, and 1 live birth, identified a novel missense variant, NM_023067:c.500T>C, p.(Phe167Ser), in a homozygous state
Since the identified missense is classified as VUS, this single variant does not allow conclusions regarding the causal role of FOXL2 in RHM

records.label: Patient 1824

phenotypes.text: androgenetic monospermic complete moles lacking p57 expression

records.segregation: Variant segregated from both heterozygous parents (second- or third-degree cousins); mother had one triploid dispermic partial mole
quotes: analysis of the exome of patient 1824 (Italian), with 2 HMs followed by secondary infertility and substantially reduced bilateral ovarian volumes (1.1 cm3 and 2.5 cm3 at the age of 25 years
revealed a novel variant affecting the splice donor of exon 6, NM_001037225.3:c.349+1G>T, in a homozygous state
The variant segregated from both parents, who are second- or third-degree cousins.

records.label: Patient 439
records.segregation: p.R519* inherited from mother; variants most likely on different parental chromosomes
quotes: analysis of the exome of patient 439 (Jordanian), with 3 HMs and 2 MCs, identified 2 variants, NM_144688:c.1555C>T, p.(Arg519*), and c.1604T>A, p.(Leu535Gln), in a heterozygous state
only one of them, p.R519*, was inherited from her mother, and therefore, the 2 variants are most likely on 2 different parental chromosomes
records.genotype_reason: two different heterozygous variants in one gene

records.label: Patient 1954
quotes: analysis of the exome of patient 1954 (Egyptian), with 4 CHMs and 2 years of primary and secondary infertility (before the first and after the third HM), identified a variant affecting the canonical acceptor splice site of exon 27, NM_014258.4:c.2530-2A>G, in a homozygous state
known consanguinity between the patient’s parents (second-degree cousins)

records.label: Proband 1802
records.segregation: Homozygous in proband and affected sister; heterozygous in both parents (third-degree cousins)
quotes: analysis of the exome of proband 1802 (Iranian), with a history of 2 HMs, identified a novel homozygous protein-truncating variant, NM_001017975:c.3124dupT, p.(Tyr1042Leufs*7)
identified the same variant in a homozygous state in the affected sister and in a heterozygous state in the 2 parents (who are third-degree cousins)

records.label: Sister of proband 1802

identified the same variant in a homozygous state in the affected sister and in a heterozygous state in the 2 parents

records.label: Maternal aunt 1922
quotes: the maternal aunt of the proband also experienced one HM at the age of 23, could not conceive, and then adopted a child.
WES on blood DNA of the maternal aunt identified a second novel LP variant by the ACMG in HFM1, c.1159-1G>A, in a heterozygous state
the maternal aunt of the proband is compound heterozygous for 2 pathogenic (P)/LP HFM1 variants

records.label: Proband 2136

records.label: Patient with FOXL2 variant
quotes: Exome sequencing identified a heterozygous deleterious variant in FOXL2 p.(Gly187Asp), reported in patients with premature ovarian insufficiency (POI)

notes.statement: By whole-exome sequencing in 2 women with recurrent hydatidiform moles, Saharan et al. (2026) identified a heterozygous FOXL2 variant (G187D), previously reported in premature ovarian insufficiency, in one patient and a very rare homozygous KASH5 variant (R196H) in the other. The authors stated that their findings further supported the association of variants in these genes with recurrent moles.
quotes: Exome sequencing identified a heterozygous deleterious variant in FOXL2 p.(Gly187Asp), reported in patients with premature ovarian insufficiency (POI), and a very rare homozygous variant in KASH5 p.(Arg196His).
Our findings further support the association of variants in these genes with RHM while highlighting the potential for severe, life-threatening progression to metastatic GTN.

notes.statement: Saharan et al. (2026) reviewed the literature for gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (GTN) rates in patients with recurrent hydatidiform moles and compared them across genetic etiologies, noting limitations of current data for interpreting overall risk.
quotes: Additionally, we reviewed the literature for GTN rates in patients with RHM and compared them between different genetic etiologies.
Reviewing GTN incidence per patient summarizes current data and their limitations that need to be taken into consideration when interpreting overall risk.

notes.statement: Rezaei et al. (2024) performed whole-exome sequencing on 75 unrelated patients with recurrent hydatidiform moles who were negative for recessive mutations in NLRP7 and KHDC3L. They found deleterious biallelic variants in genes with roles in meiosis I in patients with recurrent androgenetic complete moles. All 6 genotyped moles were androgenetic monospermic.
quotes: WES on a total of 75 unrelated patients with at least 2 HMs (including all histopathological and genotypic types), who were negative for recessive mutations in NLRP7 and KHDC3L, revealed the presence of deleterious biallelic variants in 5 genes with known roles in meiosis I in 5 unrelated probands.

Genotype analysis using multiplex and/or simplex short tandem repeat (STR) markers was performed on 6 CHMs (MAJIN, n = 2; HFM1, n = 1; FOXL2, n = 3) and demonstrated that all of them are androgenetic monospermic

notes.statement: Rezaei et al. (2024) found that 15 patients with recurrent androgenetic moles and biallelic pathogenic variants in 9 meiosis-related genes had more severe reproductive outcomes than 70 patients without biallelic variants. The 15 patients had 1 live birth and 62 pregnancy losses, compared with 39 live births and 198 losses in the 70 patients (P = 0.0007).
quotes: The 15 patients with biallelic P/LP variants had only 1 live birth (in the patient with a missense variant in FOXL2) and a total of 62 pregnancy losses (HM and MC), while the 70 patients with unexplained genetic etiology had a total of 39 live births and 198 pregnancy losses (2-tailed Fisher’s exact P value = 0.0007)

notes.statement: Rezaei et al. (2024) reported that the mother of a patient homozygous for a MAJIN splice variant was a heterozygous carrier and had a triploid dispermic partial mole at age 21. They suggested that monoallelic variants in MAJIN, and perhaps in other meiotic genes, may underlie milder phenotypes.
quotes: The mother of patient 1824, with a monoallelic P/LP variant in MAJIN, had experienced 1 HM at a young age (21 years).
Multiplex and simplex STR genotyping demonstrated a triploid dispermic genome (Supplemental Figure 14).

notes.statement: Rezaei et al. (2024) screened 494 ovarian and meiosis genes in 310 patients with reproductive loss and identified 77 monoallelic P/LP loss-of-function variants in 55 genes in 68 patients (21.8%). Variants in BRCA2 and ZP3 were significantly more frequent than in gnomAD, and genes in the DNA metabolism protein class were enriched.
quotes: This analysis led to the identification of 77 different P/LP variants in 55 genes in 68 patients (21.8%) (Supplemental Table 2).
P/LP LoF variants in BRCA2 (excluding the 2 patients with the extended splice site variant) and ZP3 were significantly more frequent in our patients

notes.statement: Rezaei et al. (2024) found that Hfm1-null fetal oocytes failed to complete synapsis and lacked MLH1 crossover foci. Hfm1-null and Majin-null ovaries showed severe oocyte loss before puberty.
quotes: By contrast, in Hfm1–/– ovaries at 17.5 dpc, only 18% of oocytes reached the pachytene stage and all the others were still at the zygotene stage
Where chromosomes were synapsed, MLH1 foci, which mark crossover sites, were absent in Hfm1–/– oocytes
By contrast, in Majin–/– and Hfm1–/– ovaries, very few oocytes remained, while FOXL2-positive granulosa cells were scattered.

notes.statement: Rezaei et al. (2024) found that surviving Hfm1-null oocytes progressed through meiosis in culture, but their spindles were often parallel to the ooplasmic membrane. Of the MII oocytes, 14% extruded all their chromosomes into the polar bodies, the same endpoint previously seen in Mei1-null oocytes. The authors proposed this as a mechanism for androgenetic mole formation.
quotes: A total of 4 out of 29 (14%) MII oocytes from Hfm1–/– females extruded all their chromosomes into polar bodies.

It is remarkable that the endpoint of Hfm1-null oocytes was similar to that of Mei1-null oocytes as we previously reported even though they do not follow exactly the same course of meiotic progression.

notes.statement: Rezaei et al. (2024) suggested that recurrent androgenetic complete moles may be a sign of accelerated ovarian aging or a milder form of premature ovarian insufficiency, providing an explanation for the increased incidence of androgenetic moles with advanced maternal age.
quotes: The data from our study suggest that recurrent AnCHM may be a sign of accelerated ovarian aging or a milder form of POI before its manifestation by clinical and laboratory tests.
